title: Naming Sides in Right-Angled Triangles — Year 9

header.title: Naming Sides in Right-Angled Triangles
header.subtitle: Hypotenuse, opposite and adjacent: it all depends on θ

meta.lesson-focus: Identify and label the hypotenuse, the side opposite a given angle, and the side adjacent to a given angle in any right-angled triangle; recognise that 'opposite' and 'adjacent' depend on the chosen reference angle; the hypotenuse is always opposite the right angle.
meta.ac9-descriptor-text: recognise the constancy of the sine, cosine and tangent ratios for a given angle in right-angled triangles using properties of similarity
meta.sa-conceptual-understanding: Trigonometric ratios are an application of the property of similarity for right-angled triangles

html.section0_intro: Today starts the trigonometry unit. These three questions check the right-angled triangle facts you already know from Year 8 and from enlargement.
html.section_warmup:
A real situation that is secretly today's mathematics.

A café owner needs a wheelchair ramp up one step. The builder quotes the handrail by the metre along the sloping ramp. The council charges rent for every metre of footpath the ramp covers. The building code limits how high the ramp may rise for its length.

Three different prices, three different sides of the same right-angled triangle. Mix them up and the quote is wrong.

Measured from the ramp angle θ: the ramp surface is the hypotenuse, the rise is opposite θ, and the footpath run is adjacent to θ. Today you learn to name these three sides in any right-angled triangle.
html.vocab_cards:
Right angle
Tap to flip
An angle of exactly 90°, marked with a small square in the corner.
Every triangle today has one.
Hypotenuse
Tap to flip
The side across from the right angle. It is always the longest side.
It never touches the square marker.
Reference angle θ
Tap to flip
The acute angle we choose to name the other two sides from. Marked with an arc.
θ is the Greek letter theta.
Opposite side
Tap to flip
The side across from θ. It does not touch θ at all.
Rise of a ramp, measured from the ramp angle.
Adjacent side
Tap to flip
The side that touches θ and is not the hypotenuse.
Adjacent means 'next to'.

html.section4_heading: Name the side from the letters
html.worked_example:
Name the hypotenuse, the opposite side and the adjacent side of triangle KLM for the reference angle θ at K.

1
Find the right angle, name the hypotenuse
The square marker is at L. The hypotenuse is the side that does not touch L.
Right angle at L  →  hypotenuse = KM = 13 cm (the longest side ✓)
2
Find θ, name the opposite side
θ is at K. The opposite side is the one that does not touch K.
θ at K  →  opposite = LM = 5 cm
3
The side left over is adjacent
KL touches θ at K and is not the hypotenuse, so it is adjacent. Check: it joins θ to the right angle.
Hypotenuse KM = 13 cm
Opposite LM = 5 cm
Adjacent KL = 12 cm
Answer Hyp = KM  ·  Opp = LM  ·  Adj = KL. If θ moved to M, opposite and adjacent would swap; KM stays the hypotenuse.
html.section6_heading: We do: triangle RST, turned on its side
html.we_do_intro: This triangle is turned so the hypotenuse is not at the bottom. Work through each prompt with a partner, then we check as a class. Answer side names in alphabetical order.
html.strategy_section:
★Spot the mistake

Jordan labelled triangle PQR for θ at R. Click the line where the mistake first appears.

Right angle at Q, θ at R. Name the hypotenuse, adjacent and opposite sides.
1 The right angle is at Q, so the hypotenuse is PR = 15 cm.
2 θ is at R. PR touches R, so the adjacent side is PR = 15 cm.
3 The opposite side is the one left over: QR = 12 cm.

✓ Right: that's where the mistake first appears.

Why: PR does touch θ, but it was already named the hypotenuse in line 1. The hypotenuse is never called adjacent. The adjacent side touches θ and the right angle: QR. That leaves PQ as the opposite side.

Now fix line 2: how long is the adjacent side, in cm?

★Hinge check 🎯 Pick one

The triangle is tilted. The right angle is at B and θ is at C. Which side is adjacent to θ?

Not quite: AC is the hypotenuse. It touches θ, but it is across from the right angle at B, so it keeps the name hypotenuse. Adjacent is the other side touching θ.
Correct. BC touches θ at C and also touches the right angle at B. AC is the hypotenuse and AB is opposite θ.
That's the opposite side. AB does not touch C at all, so it is across from θ. Adjacent means it touches θ.
Turning the triangle changes nothing. The names come from where the right angle and θ are, not from which side is at the bottom. BC is adjacent however the triangle is drawn.

retrieval.q: A right-angled triangle has one angle of 35°. What is the size of the third angle, in degrees?
retrieval.hint: Angles in a triangle add to 180°, and one of them is 90°: 180 − 90 − 35.

fb.145: You only took 35 away from 180. The right angle uses up another 90°.

retrieval.q: A right-angled triangle has shorter sides 6 cm and 8 cm. How long is the longest side, in cm? (Pythagoras)

fb.14: You added the sides. Pythagoras adds the squares: 6² + 8², then square-root.
fb.100: 100 is the square of the longest side. Take the square root.

retrieval.q: A triangle with sides 3 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm is enlarged by scale factor 3. How long is the image of the 4 cm side, in cm?
retrieval.hint: Every length is multiplied by the scale factor.

fb.7: An enlargement multiplies lengths by the scale factor; it does not add to them.

matchTerms.html:
△PQR, right angle at Q, θ at P.
Opposite θ?

△XYZ, right angle at X, θ at Z.
Adjacent to θ?

△LMN, right angle at N, θ at L.
Opposite θ?

△DEF, right angle at E, θ at F.
Adjacent to θ?

weDo.q: Which side is the hypotenuse? Type the two letters in alphabetical order (e.g. AB, not BA).
weDo.hint: Find the right-angle marker at S. The hypotenuse is the side that does not touch S.

fb.RS: RS touches the right angle at S. The hypotenuse is across from the right angle.

weDo.q: Same triangle, θ at T. How long is the side opposite θ, in cm?
weDo.hint: The opposite side is the one that does not touch T at all.

fb.15: ST touches T, so it is the adjacent side, not the opposite side.
fb.17: RT is the hypotenuse. It touches T but it is never called adjacent or opposite.

weDo.q: Now make the angle at R the reference angle instead. How long is the side opposite R, in cm?
weDo.hint: Which side does not touch R at all?

fb.8: 8 cm was opposite T. When the reference angle moves to R, opposite and adjacent swap.

checkpoint.q: How long is the hypotenuse, in cm?
checkpoint.hint: The hypotenuse is across from the right angle at Q, and it is the longest side.

checkpoint.q: Same triangle, θ at R. How long is the side adjacent to θ, in cm?
checkpoint.hint: Adjacent touches R but is not the hypotenuse.

fb.17: PR touches R, but it is the hypotenuse. Adjacent is the other side that touches θ.
fb.15: PQ does not touch R, so it is the opposite side.

practice1.hint: The right angle is at E, so look for the side without E.

fb.DE: DE touches the right angle at E. The hypotenuse is across from it.

practice1.q: Which side is opposite θ? Type the two letters in alphabetical order (e.g. AB, not BA).
practice1.hint: θ is at G. The opposite side is the one that does not touch G.

fb.GH: GH touches θ, so it is the adjacent side.

practice1.q: Which side is adjacent to θ? Type the two letters in alphabetical order (e.g. AB, not BA).
practice1.hint: Adjacent touches θ (at G) and is not the hypotenuse.

fb.GJ: GJ touches θ, but it is the hypotenuse, so it is not called adjacent.

practice1.q: Side MN is ___ θ. Type hypotenuse, opposite or adjacent.
practice1.hint: Does MN touch P, where θ is?

fb.adjacent: MN does not touch P at all, so it cannot be adjacent to θ.

practice1.q: Same triangle MNP. Side NP is the ___ side. Type hypotenuse, opposite or adjacent.
practice1.hint: NP touches θ at P and also touches the right angle at N.

practice1.q: Same triangle MNP. How long is the hypotenuse, in cm?
practice1.hint: Across from the right angle at N: side MP.

practice1.q: How long is the side opposite θ, in cm?
practice1.hint: θ is at U. Which side does not touch U?

fb.7: TU touches θ at U, so it is the adjacent side.
fb.25: SU is across from the right angle, so it is the hypotenuse.

practice1.q: Same triangle STU. How long is the side adjacent to θ, in cm?
practice1.hint: Adjacent touches U and is not the hypotenuse.

practice1.q: In any right-angled triangle, the hypotenuse is always the ___ side. Type longest or shortest.
practice1.hint: It sits across from the biggest angle, the 90° angle.

practice2.q: The triangle is turned so the hypotenuse is not at the bottom. How long is the side opposite θ, in cm?
practice2.hint: Ignore which way the triangle is turned. θ is at V; find the side that does not touch V.

fb.9: VW touches θ at V, so it is adjacent.

practice2.q: Same triangle VWX. Now use the angle at X as the reference angle. How long is the side adjacent to X, in cm?
practice2.hint: Adjacent to X touches X and is not the hypotenuse.

fb.15: VX is still the hypotenuse; it never changes name.
fb.9: VW does not touch X, so it is opposite X.

practice2.q: No diagram: △PQR has its right angle at R and θ at Q. Which side is opposite θ? Type the two letters in alphabetical order (e.g. AB, not BA).
practice2.hint: Opposite θ means the side that does not contain the letter Q.

fb.PQ: PQ is across from the right angle at R, so it is the hypotenuse.

practice2.q: No diagram: △JKL has its right angle at K and θ at L. Which side is adjacent to θ? Type the two letters in alphabetical order (e.g. AB, not BA).
practice2.hint: Adjacent contains both letters: the θ vertex (L) and the right-angle vertex (K).

fb.JL: JL is across from the right angle at K, so it is the hypotenuse.

practice2.q: In △ABC the angles are A = 90°, B = 30° and C = 60°. The reference angle is the 30° angle. Which side is opposite it? Type the two letters in alphabetical order (e.g. AB, not BA).
practice2.hint: The 30° angle is at B. Which side does not touch B?

fb.BC: BC is across from the 90° angle at A, so it is the hypotenuse.
fb.AB: AB touches B, so it is adjacent.

practice2.q: Both shorter sides are 5 m. With θ at X, which side is opposite θ? Type the two letters in alphabetical order (e.g. AB, not BA).
practice2.hint: Equal lengths do not decide the name; position does. Which side does not touch X?

fb.XZ: XZ touches θ at X, so it is adjacent, even though it is also 5 m.

practice3.q: Café ramp. A café is quoted $90 per metre for a handrail that runs along the sloping ramp surface (the hypotenuse). What does the handrail cost, in dollars?
practice3.hint: Pick the hypotenuse (across from the right angle), then multiply its length by 90.

fb.540: 6.00 m is the run along the ground (adjacent). The handrail follows the ramp surface, the hypotenuse.
fb.45: 0.50 m is the rise (opposite θ). The handrail follows the hypotenuse.

practice3.q: Same ramp. Council charges $120 per metre of footpath used, measured along the ground: the side adjacent to the ramp angle θ. What is the council charge, in dollars?
practice3.hint: The adjacent side touches θ (at A) and is not the hypotenuse: AB.

fb.722.4: 6.02 m is the hypotenuse, the sloping ramp. The footpath is measured along the ground (adjacent).

practice3.q: Work out oppositehypotenuse for θ. Type a decimal.
practice3.hint: Opposite θ is QR = 6 cm (it does not touch P). Hypotenuse is 10 cm. 6 ÷ 10.

fb.0.8: 8 cm is PR, which touches θ: that is the adjacent side, not the opposite.
fb.0.75: You used the adjacent side (8 cm) on the bottom. The hypotenuse goes on the bottom.

practice3.q: The triangle in the last question is enlarged by scale factor 2.5, so its sides become 20 cm, 15 cm and 25 cm. θ does not change. Work out oppositehypotenuse for θ in the enlarged triangle. Type a decimal.
practice3.hint: Opposite is now 6 × 2.5 = 15 cm, hypotenuse 10 × 2.5 = 25 cm. 15 ÷ 25.

fb.0.75: 20 cm is adjacent to θ. The hypotenuse (25 cm) goes on the bottom.
fb.0.8: 20 cm is the image of the 8 cm side, which is adjacent to θ, not opposite.

exitProbs.hint: The right angle is at F; the hypotenuse does not touch F.

exitProbs.q: Same triangle EFG, θ at G. How long is the side adjacent to θ, in cm?
exitProbs.hint: Adjacent touches G and is not the hypotenuse.

fb.13: EG touches θ, but it is the hypotenuse, not the adjacent side.
fb.5: EF does not touch G, so it is opposite θ.

exitProbs.q: Explain why the opposite and adjacent sides swap names when the reference angle moves to the other acute angle, but the hypotenuse keeps its name.
exitProbs.hint: Opposite and adjacent are named from θ; the hypotenuse is named from the right angle.
